name: Stonewall Inn
scope: Street exteriors of 51–53 Christopher Street, their contrasting upper facades and storefront signs; no interiors or crowd sculpture.
era: surviving exterior represented by selected dated references

stories.title: The Stonewall Inn: From Horse Stables to Hallowed Ground

references.caption: Outside of the official business district, the Stonewall Inn, a gay bar on Christopher Street in Manhattan's Greenwich Village. A 1969 police raid here led to the Stonewall riots, one of the most important events in the history of LGBT rights (and the history of the United States). This picture was taken on pride weekend in 2016, the day after President Obama announced the Stonewall National Monument, and less than two weeks after the Pulse nightclub shooting in Orlando.

review.method: Both selected original local photographs inspected individually at full available resolution, supplemented by individually inspected official designation photo/map and current NPS visitor-center photograph.
review.notes: Local 2016 and 2014 photographs establish the 53 facade, windows, baskets, arches and storefront. 51 uses the official four-window description and post-2024 visitor-center photo. Dated temporary banners, crowd and old salon signage excluded. Rear roof details remain conservative approximations.
